Convert a Received Frame to an Arrow Stream

Source: R/arrow.R
mizu_as_arrow.Rd

mizu_as_arrow() converts a data frame — typically one received over a channel — into a struct-typed nanoarrow_array_stream, ready for nanoarrow::convert_array_stream(), arrow::as_arrow_table(), or any other Arrow C Data Interface consumer.

Usage

mizu_as_arrow(x)

Arguments

x

a data frame.

Value

A struct-typed nanoarrow_array_stream.

Details

Columns still backed by their received shared-memory pages export zero-copy: the stream's buffers point straight into the shared region for attribute-free double, integer, integer64, and character views (character as large_string). Everything else — factors, Date / POSIXct / difftime columns, logical and raw vectors, and materialized or never-shared columns — converts per column through nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array(). The shared region stays mapped until the stream and every array produced from it are fully released.

Examples

ch <- mizu_channel(quote(mizu_send(ch, mizu_recv(ch))))
mizu_send(ch, arrow::arrow_table(data.frame(x = runif(1e5), s = "a")))
df <- mizu_recv(ch, timeout = 30)
stream <- mizu_as_arrow(df)
arrow::as_arrow_table(stream)
#> Table
#> 100000 rows x 2 columns
#> $x <double>
#> $s <large_string>
mizu_close(ch)
